note: Grievances, front pages and applications are office-free or carry their own office; run-up and rallies are the president's. Apologies have no office field in format.ts, so check.ts cannot see their byOffice split: apo-steps is the mayor's, apo-briefly the governor's, apo-humbly the president's (by id).

grievances.text: No more pumpkins until you return our ribbon scissors. You know which scissors.
grievances.subject: ribbons

grievances.text: You posed with our bus stop and kept it. We now wait at a lamp post.
grievances.subject: buses

grievances.text: No displays until our mirror is back. You were only going to check your hat.
grievances.subject: vanity

grievances.text: No practice until our room is back. Your portrait sitting is in its sixth week.
grievances.subject: portraits

grievances.text: No buses logged until our logbook is back. You signed every page, then the cover.
grievances.subject: buses

grievances.text: Bare windows until the hat from window four is back. It suited the stand better.
grievances.subject: hats

grievances.text: No sitting until our QUIET PLEASE sign is back. You held it up at your speech.
grievances.subject: signage

grievances.text: No weigh-in until our first-prize rosette is back. You did not enter.
grievances.subject: vegetable-shows

grievances.text: Our best kite was lent for a photograph. It is now framed in your hall.
grievances.subject: kites

grievances.text: No concerts until our music stands come back. They are holding up your portraits.
grievances.subject: portraits

grievances.text: Our show hedge went behind you in a photograph. It has not come back.
grievances.subject: hedges

grievances.text: No trimming until our spirit level is back. Your nameplate is straight now.
grievances.subject: hedges

grievances.text: No launches until our string is back. You keep cutting it at openings.
grievances.subject: ribbons

grievances.text: We will not sit until the pond gets its name back. It never asked for yours.
grievances.subject: vanity

frontPages.text: MAYOR'S GOOSE GIVEN OWN PARKING SPACE. Goose declines to comment.
frontPages.subject: geese

frontPages.text: MAYOR HOLDS OPENING FOR NEW SCISSORS. Old scissors not invited.
frontPages.subject: ribbons

frontPages.text: MAYOR ARRIVES EARLY TO OWN WELCOME. Waits to be welcomed.
frontPages.subject: ceremonies

frontPages.text: MAYOR'S NAME FOUND ON 41 BENCHES. Town has 40 benches.
frontPages.subject: vanity

frontPages.text: MAYOR SENDS HAT TO RIBBON-CUTTING. Ribbon cut on time, for once.
frontPages.subject: hats

frontPages.text: MAYOR WRITES SELF A THANK-YOU CARD. Replies the same day.
frontPages.subject: vanity

frontPages.text: GOVERNOR THANKS GOVERNOR 14 TIMES IN SPEECH. Audience thanked once.
frontPages.subject: vanity

frontPages.text: GOVERNOR UNVEILS PLAQUE TO UNVEILING OF PLAQUE. Another planned.
frontPages.subject: ceremonies

frontPages.text: GOVERNOR REOPENS FOOTBRIDGE FOR THIRD TIME. It had never closed.
frontPages.subject: ceremonies

frontPages.text: GOVERNOR CUTS ONE RIBBON NINE TIMES FOR CAMERAS. Ribbon now confetti.
frontPages.subject: ribbons

frontPages.text: GOVERNOR POSES WITH PHOTOGRAPH OF GOVERNOR. Both 'looking well'.
frontPages.subject: portraits

frontPages.text: GOVERNOR FILLS IN FORM REQUESTING OWN AUTOGRAPH. Request granted.
frontPages.subject: paperwork

frontPages.text: PRESIDENT'S SIGNATURE NOW THREE PAGES WIDE. Law fits on a fourth.
frontPages.subject: paperwork

frontPages.text: PRESIDENT AWARDS SELF THE FOLDED NAPKIN. Accepts, graciously.
frontPages.subject: ceremonies

frontPages.text: PRESIDENT REHEARSES OWN SURPRISE BIRTHDAY. 'Very convincing'.
frontPages.subject: vanity

frontPages.text: PRESIDENT'S CAKE GETS PRESS OFFICER. Cake 'not taking questions'.
frontPages.subject: vanity

frontPages.text: PRESIDENT NAMES CLOUD AFTER SELF. Cloud moves on.
frontPages.subject: picnic-weather

frontPages.text: PRESIDENT'S NAME ADDED TO DICTIONARY. Defined as 'see ribbon'.
frontPages.subject: ribbons

frontPages.text: PRESIDENT PRACTISES HANDSHAKE ON DOOR. Door 'warmly received'.
frontPages.subject: ceremonies

frontPages.text: PRESIDENT HAS CARPET ROLLED OUT TO KETTLE. Tea takes an hour.
frontPages.subject: ceremonies

apologies.note: mayor (the specification's 'Apologise on the steps' does not fit the label box, and mayor-4 owns the town hall steps)

applications.text: I apply to be your minister. References: 'She found one.'
applications.returnText: I apply again. Since last time, I have found another one.

applications.text: I ended the onion dispute. Both onions are speaking again.
applications.returnText: I apply again. The onions asked after you.
applications.note: Vegetables; settlements x0.5: she calms quarrels

applications.text: I can find a sponsor for anything. I once found one for a puddle.
applications.returnText: I apply again. The puddle still speaks well of me.

applications.text: Rumours lose interest when I walk in. I am never talked about.
applications.returnText: I apply again. Nobody mentioned I had gone.

applications.text: I have played at 212 ribbon-cuttings. I know when the scissors close.
applications.returnText: I apply again. I have kept the fanfare warm.

applications.text: I can open a fête with a third of the fuss. I bring my own chair.
applications.returnText: I apply again. The chair is already unfolded.

applications.text: I once kept a kite up for nine hours. I was asked for one.
applications.returnText: I apply again. The kite is still up.

applications.text: I have said nothing, very well, for thirty years.
applications.returnText: I apply again. I did not mention it to anyone.

applications.text: I have patched the same waders for twenty years. They are now all patch.
applications.returnText: I apply again. In the same waders.

runUp.text: Hold the {district} ribbon. Someone else cuts it. Smile anyway.
runUp.subject: ribbons

runUp.text: Open the {district} band festival. The band will play you in. Then out.
runUp.subject: bandstands

runUp.text: Present the {district} cup. It reads: THE PRESIDENT, AND THE WINNER.
runUp.subject: ceremonies

runUp.text: Inspect the {district} fishing pegs. Nod. Nodding has a form.
runUp.subject: paperwork

runUp.text: Sit for the {district} art club. They asked for a bowl of fruit.
runUp.subject: portraits

runUp.text: Read the {district} timetable aloud. All of it. Mervyn checks.
runUp.subject: buses

runUp.text: Take questions at the {district} parrot show. Answer each one twice.
runUp.subject: ceremonies

runUp.text: Pose by the oldest tree in {district}. Look wise. It will cope.
runUp.subject: gardens

runUp.text: Take tea at Till's Teas in {district}. Keep the name showing.
runUp.subject: vanity

runUp.text: Throw a hoop at the {district} fair. Three cameras. One go.
runUp.subject: ceremonies

runUp.text: Unveil the {district} weathervane. It points at you, as arranged.
runUp.subject: signage

runUp.text: Judge the {district} Quiet Competition. Applaud in silence.
runUp.subject: ceremonies

runUp.text: Start the {district} duck race. The ducks have been briefed.
runUp.subject: ducks

runUp.text: Launch the {district} kite. You hold it up. Philomena runs.
runUp.subject: kites

runUp.text: Unveil a copy of the founding napkin in {district}. Do not use it.
runUp.subject: paperwork

runUp.text: Unveil the {district} hedge sign. It is a hedge, trimmed to read HEDGE.
runUp.subject: signage

runUp.text: Open the {district} flower show. Smell all 400 roses.
runUp.subject: gardens

runUp.text: Open the {district} library. Your book is on loan. To you.
runUp.subject: vanity

runUp.text: Judge the {district} dog show. Rodney has taught one to wave.
runUp.subject: ceremonies

runUp.text: Cut the {district} cheese. A ribbon has been tied round it.
runUp.subject: ribbons

runUp.text: Judge the {district} shop windows. You are in all twelve.
runUp.subject: vanity

runUp.text: Tour the {district} allotments. Hilda introduces each onion.
runUp.subject: vegetable-shows

runUp.text: Open the {district} model railway. Tiny ribbon, tiny scissors, same smile.
runUp.subject: ribbons

runUp.text: Ring the {district} bell once. Then once for the photograph.
runUp.subject: ceremonies

rallies.text: A rally at the kite festival. Cut the ribbon on a kite. Watch it go.
rallies.subject: ribbons

rallies.text: A rally at the bandstand. Your scissors arrive in a box, in a box.
rallies.subject: ribbons

rallies.text: A rally at the hedge show. Bring shears. Agnes will say which leaf.
rallies.subject: hedges

rallies.text: A rally at the fête. Rodney has brought nine ribbons, in case.
rallies.subject: ribbons
